Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear questions, happy to confirm options and constraints. High level answers first, then specifics.

High level:
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ (we recommend TLS 1.3) for all client-server connections and intra-service traffic.
- At-rest: AES-256-GCM for model artifacts and persisted data; envelope encryption is used with a data key protected by a KMS CMK.
- CMK options: (1) Redwood-managed KMS (default), (2) Customer-managed KMS (BYOK) in customer's AWS account with cross-account grants, (3) Dedicated/private deployment where you can bring CloudHSM-backed keys.
- HSM: For FIPS-level HSM backing we support CloudHSM in Dedicated/Private deployments; we can also integrate with customer HSMs in certain air-gapped/on-prem setups (requires additional onboarding).
- Key usage logging: KMS/CloudTrail events can be forwarded to your SIEM; decryption events are logged as KMS API calls (no plaintext in CloudTrail).
- Plaintext handling: Redwood does not persist unencrypted plaintext of PII. Decrypted data exists only transiently in-memory for inference; we can present a design for memory hardening and process-level isolation for PHI flows.

Specifics to your numbered items:
1) Cross-account CMK: Supported. You can create a CMK in your account (us-east-1) and grant Redwood's service principal decrypt/encrypt permissions. We support both grant-based (recommended) and key policy approaches. Note: cross-account grants mean Redwood never has direct control of your CMK; permissions are explicit.
2) HSM requirement: CloudHSM-backed CMKs are supported but generally require Dedicated or Private deployment because the HSM needs network isolation and tenancy. For most customers who need FIPS-backed keys we recommend a Dedicated pool in the customer's region with an attached CloudHSM cluster.
3) Logging & plaintext: We do not write plaintext PII to logs. KMS usage is logged via CloudTrail; we can configure log forwarding to your SIEM and provide a sample retention/archival plan. For additional assurance, we offer a configurable masking/tokenization layer and can limit debug-level logs for your tenant.
4) Data residency: For strict, single-region residency (no replication), the safest path is Redwood Dedicated in us-east-1 or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). Our hosted offering can be constrained to regionally pinned infrastructure for many customers, but for contractual residency guarantees we recommend Dedicated/Private.
